news.title: Umejiaku Dedicates U-17 World Cup Golden Ball to Soludo
news.lede: The Flamingos forward handed her Golden Ball tribute to the Anambra governor in Abuja, days after Nigeria became the first African nation to win the U-17 Women’s World Cup. Oluebube Umejiaku has dedicated her Player of the Tournament award from the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup to Anambra State Governor, Prof Chukwuma Charles Soludo.

news.title: Spain's prime minister ignites war over the 2030 World Cup final with Morocco
news.lede: "We won in New York and we will win in Madrid"Fiery remarks from Pedro Sánchez have reignited the debate over the 2030 World Cup. The Spanish Prime Minister recalled the moment his national team collected the World Cup trophy in the United States, describing the sight of US President Donald Trump handing it to Spain as "a genuine political orgasm". His comments landed as the row over where the final will be staged intensifies: Spain or Morocco? Speaking to " La Séptima " radio, Sánchez defended the joint bid by Spain, Portugal and Morocco to host the 2030 tournament, stressing that the original initiative came from the two Iberian nations."

news.title: Flamingos’ World Cup title puts NFF reform under spotlight as Jalla seeks role for ex-players
news.lede: Nigeria’s Flamingos have conquered the world, but their historic triumph has also brought fresh attention to a major question facing Nigerian football: who should take charge of the game’s administration? The Flamingos defeated Japan 2-1 in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Rabat, Morocco, on Saturday, November 7, becoming the first African women’s national team to win a FIFA World Cup title at any age level. Awawu Bashiru opened the scoring in the 39th minute before Oluebube Umejiaku doubled Nigeria’s lead two minutes into the second half. Japan pulled one back through Fuki Ito in the 80th minute, but the Nigerian girls held on to secure the trophy.

news.title: 2026 Amputee World Cup: Ghana name final 15-man squad
news.lede: Ghana's national amputee football team, the Black Challenge, have named their final 15-man squad for the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup, scheduled for November 13–22 in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico. Head coach Stephen Richard Obeng has selected three goalkeepers, four defenders, four midfielders and four forwards for the tournament. The squad includes Richard Ekwam, Hamza Mohammed, Yussif Yahaya and Fuseini Iddi, alongside goalkeepers Atsu Abor, Richmond Ofosu and Razak Seidu. 11 out of the current 15 players were also part of Ghana's squad for the 2024 African Amputee Football Cup of Nations in Egypt, where the Black Challenge successfully defended their continental title.

news.title: Black Challenge names 15-man squad for 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico
news.lede: Ghana’s Black Challenge head coach, Stephen Richard Obeng, has unveiled his final 15-man squad for the 2026 WAFF Men’s Amputee Football World Cup, with the team scheduled to depart for Mexico on Tuesday, November 10. The squad features three goalkeepers and 12 outfield players who will carry Ghana’s hopes at the tournament, which runs from November 13 to 22 in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico. The Black Challenge will compete with financial support from Gold Fields, while the Football Association has reiterated its commitment to the team’s campaign in partnership with the National Amputee Football Association of Ghana and the Ministry of Sports and Recreation. A total of 24 national teams from Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas will compete for the title.
